source.original_text: Literal Eq14/15 component definition, with the explicit deterministic polynomial extension off the sphere. For positive integer n, natural h, 0<=i<=h and even 4<=p<=P, set K=2^(74(h+1)), P=2^(64(h+1)), S_i=sum_{j=0}^{h-i}K^j, a_i,p=1/[p^4*S_i^2*sqrt((h-i+1)*log(2*P*S_i))]. For any real direction vectors and coefficient array, take psi_i=u_i tensor u_(i+1)^tensor K tensor ... tensor u_h^tensor K^(h-i), and define F_i,p=sqrt(n)*a_i,p*<Xi_i,p,psi_i^tensor p> using the full ordered entrywise real tensor pairing. The source uses unit directions and sufficiently large n with its prescribed h; no probability law is claimed by the definition.

fun (n : ℕ+) (h : ℕ) (i : Fin (h + 1))
    (p : {p : ℕ // Even p ∧ 4 ≤ p ∧ p ≤ 2 ^ (64 * (h + 1))})
    (u : Fin (h - i.val + 1) → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n.val))
    (ξ : EuclideanSpace ℝ
      ((Fin p.val × (Σ j : Fin (h - i.val + 1),
        Fin ((2 ^ (74 * (h + 1))) ^ j.val))) → Fin n.val)) ↦
  let S : ℕ := ∑ j : Fin (h - i.val + 1), (2 ^ (74 * (h + 1))) ^ j.val
  let a : ℝ := 1 / ((p.val : ℝ) ^ 4 * (S : ℝ) ^ 2 *
    Real.sqrt ((h - i.val + 1 : ℕ) * Real.log (2 * (2 : ℝ) ^ (64 * (h + 1)) * S)))
  Real.sqrt n.val * a * ∑ c, ξ c * ∏ s, u s.2.1 (c s)

blind_reconstruction.text: Definition (not a theorem). Let n be a positive integer, h a nonnegative integer, i an integer with 0 <= i <= h, and p an even integer satisfying 4 <= p <= Q, where Q = 2^(64(h+1)). Put m = h-i+1 (the displayed natural subtraction is truncated), B = 2^(74(h+1)), S = sum_{j=0}^{m-1} B^j, and a = 1 / [p^4 S^2 sqrt(m log(2 Q S))], with natural-number quantities interpreted as reals in this formula and log the natural logarithm. Let T = {(r,j,k) : 0 <= r < p, 0 <= j < m, 0 <= k < B^j}, and let C be the set of all functions c:T -> {0,...,n-1}. For any tuple u = (u_0,...,u_{m-1}) of vectors in R^n and any coefficient vector xi in the real Euclidean space R^C, the displayed expression defines the real-valued function F by F(n,h,i,p,u,xi) = sqrt(n) a sum_{c in C} xi_c product_{r=0}^{p-1} product_{j=0}^{m-1} product_{k=0}^{B^j-1} (u_j)_{c(r,j,k)}. Thus there are p S slots, and the direction u_j is used in p B^j slots. There is no unit-norm assumption on u and no probability measure, law, inequality, or theorem conclusion asserted by this expression.

import Mathlib.Probability.Distributions.Gaussian.Multivariate
import Mathlib.Probability.HasLaw
import Mathlib.Data.PNat.Basic

/-!
# The actual Gaussian angular degree component

Zhou–Suzuki, arXiv:2611.05813v1 (CC BY 4.0), Section 4.1.1, Eq. (14)–(15).
Tensor coordinates are indexed by a choice in each repeated tensor slot. This
retains the ordered tensor, its multiplicities and the exact source amplitude.
The law is for deterministic unit directions under one actual standard Gaussian
coefficient block. Joint coefficient independence, degree summation, radial
cutoffs and conditional level iteration are separate obligations.

The isolated identity permits every positive dimension and natural depth; it
does not assert hard-family admissibility outside the source parameter regime.
The literal polynomial extends to arbitrary directions, but its Gaussian law
below uses only the source sphere domain.
-/

open MeasureTheory ProbabilityTheory
open scoped BigOperators

namespace AutoSamplingTheory.ExampleCases.SlcLsiQueryComplexity.AngularDegree

/-- The literal Eq. (15) degree component, including the Eq. (14) amplitude.
The tensor slots select a copy of `psi`, then a trailing block and repetition.
Only its restriction to unit directions is used by the source-law theorem. -/
noncomputable def angularDegreeComponent (n : ℕ+) (h : ℕ) (i : Fin (h + 1))
    (p : {p : ℕ // Even p ∧ 4 ≤ p ∧ p ≤ 2 ^ (64 * (h + 1))})
    (u : Fin (h - i.val + 1) → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n.val))
    (ξ : EuclideanSpace ℝ
      ((Fin p.val × (Σ j : Fin (h - i.val + 1),
        Fin ((2 ^ (74 * (h + 1))) ^ j.val))) → Fin n.val)) : ℝ :=
  let S : ℕ := ∑ j : Fin (h - i.val + 1), (2 ^ (74 * (h + 1))) ^ j.val
  let a : ℝ := 1 / ((p.val : ℝ) ^ 4 * (S : ℝ) ^ 2 *
    Real.sqrt ((h - i.val + 1 : ℕ) * Real.log (2 * (2 : ℝ) ^ (64 * (h + 1)) * S)))
  Real.sqrt n.val * a * ∑ c, ξ c * ∏ s, u s.2.1 (c s)

private abbrev TensorSlots (h : ℕ) (i : Fin (h + 1)) (p : ℕ) :=
  Fin p × (Σ j : Fin (h - i.val + 1), Fin ((2 ^ (74 * (h + 1))) ^ j.val))

private noncomputable def tensorFeature (n : ℕ+) (h : ℕ) (i : Fin (h + 1)) (p : ℕ)
    (u : Fin (h - i.val + 1) → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n.val)) :
    EuclideanSpace ℝ (TensorSlots h i p → Fin n.val) :=
  WithLp.toLp 2 fun c ↦ ∏ s, u s.2.1 (c s)

private theorem tensorFeature_norm_sq (n : ℕ+) (h : ℕ) (i : Fin (h + 1)) (p : ℕ)
    (u : Fin (h - i.val + 1) → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n.val))
    (hu : ∀ j, ‖u j‖ = 1) : ‖tensorFeature n h i p u‖ ^ 2 = 1 := by
  rw [EuclideanSpace.real_norm_sq_eq]
  change (∑ c : TensorSlots h i p → Fin n.val,
    (∏ s : TensorSlots h i p, u s.2.1 (c s)) ^ 2) = 1
  simp_rw [← Finset.prod_pow]
  rw [← Fintype.prod_sum (fun (s : TensorSlots h i p) (k : Fin n.val) ↦
    (u s.2.1 k) ^ 2)]
  simp_rw [← EuclideanSpace.real_norm_sq_eq, hu]
  simp

/-- At fixed unit directions the actual Gaussian tensor polynomial has the
source centered normal law with variance `n * a²`. This proves measurability and
the law; neither a Gaussian-law witness nor tensor normalization is assumed. -/
theorem angularDegreeComponent_hasLaw (n : ℕ+) (h : ℕ) (i : Fin (h + 1))
    (p : {p : ℕ // Even p ∧ 4 ≤ p ∧ p ≤ 2 ^ (64 * (h + 1))})
    (u : Fin (h - i.val + 1) → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n.val))
    (hu : ∀ j, ‖u j‖ = 1) :
    let S : ℕ := ∑ j : Fin (h - i.val + 1), (2 ^ (74 * (h + 1))) ^ j.val
    let a : ℝ := 1 / ((p.val : ℝ) ^ 4 * (S : ℝ) ^ 2 *
      Real.sqrt ((h - i.val + 1 : ℕ) * Real.log (2 * (2 : ℝ) ^ (64 * (h + 1)) * S)))
    HasLaw (angularDegreeComponent n h i p u)
      (gaussianReal 0 (((n.val : ℝ) * a ^ 2).toNNReal)) (stdGaussian _) := by
  let S : ℕ := ∑ j : Fin (h - i.val + 1), (2 ^ (74 * (h + 1))) ^ j.val
  let a : ℝ := 1 / ((p.val : ℝ) ^ 4 * (S : ℝ) ^ 2 *
    Real.sqrt ((h - i.val + 1 : ℕ) * Real.log (2 * (2 : ℝ) ^ (64 * (h + 1)) * S)))
  let L : StrongDual ℝ (EuclideanSpace ℝ (TensorSlots h i p.val → Fin n.val)) :=
    (Real.sqrt n.val * a) • innerSL ℝ (tensorFeature n h i p.val u)
  change HasLaw (angularDegreeComponent n h i p u)
    (gaussianReal 0 (((n.val : ℝ) * a ^ 2).toNNReal)) (stdGaussian _)
  have hL : (fun ξ ↦ L ξ) = angularDegreeComponent n h i p u := by
    funext ξ
    change (Real.sqrt n.val * a) * inner ℝ (tensorFeature n h i p.val u) ξ =
      (Real.sqrt n.val * a) * ∑ c, ξ c * ∏ s, u s.2.1 (c s)
    congr 1
  have hnorm : ‖L‖ ^ 2 = (n.val : ℝ) * a ^ 2 := by
    simp only [L, norm_smul, innerSL_apply_norm, mul_pow, Real.norm_eq_abs, sq_abs]
    rw [tensorFeature_norm_sq n h i p.val u hu, mul_one,
      Real.sq_sqrt (Nat.cast_nonneg n.val)]
  rw [← hL]
  refine ⟨L.continuous.aemeasurable, ?_⟩
  rw [IsGaussian.map_eq_gaussianReal, integral_strongDual_stdGaussian,
    variance_dual_stdGaussian, hnorm]

end AutoSamplingTheory.ExampleCases.SlcLsiQueryComplexity.AngularDegree

candidate_publication_context.statement: In the source construction n is sufficiently large and h=floor((log n)^(1/3)/32). Set K=2^(74(h+1)), P=2^(64(h+1)), S_i=Σ_{j=0}^{h−i}K^j, and a_i,p=1/[p^4 S_i² sqrt((h−i+1)log(2PS_i))]. For 0≤i≤h and even 4≤p≤P, take deterministic unit directions u_i,…,u_h and the ordered tensor ψ_i=u_i⊗u_(i+1)^⊗K⊗⋯⊗u_h^⊗K^(h−i). A standard Gaussian coefficient tensor Ξ_i,p in real Euclidean dimension n^(pS_i) defines F_i,p=√n a_i,p⟨Ξ_i,p,ψ_i^⊗p⟩. At each fixed direction tuple, F_i,p has law N(0,n a_i,p²). The isolated formal identity is valid for every positive n and natural h; joint independence and the degree-summed field are not covered here.

formulae.label: Ordered tensor and component
formulae.tex: \psi_i=u_i\otimes u_{i+1}^{\otimes K}\otimes\cdots\otimes u_h^{\otimes K^{h-i}},\qquad F_{i,p}^{\Xi}(u)=\sqrt n\,a_{i,p}\langle\Xi_{i,p},\psi_i(u)^{\otimes p}\rangle.

assumptions: n is a positive integer, h a nonnegative integer, 0≤i≤h, and p is even with 4≤p≤P.
The trailing directions u_i,…,u_h are fixed deterministic unit vectors in real Euclidean n-space.
The coefficient block has its unconditioned standard Gaussian probability law; it is not conditioned on admissibility.
The paper fixes sufficiently large n and h=floor((log n)^(1/3)/32). The isolated identity below is proved for every positive n and natural h; this does not extend hard-family admissibility.

lesson.title: Construct one angular degree component
assumptions: n is a positive integer, h a nonnegative integer, 0≤i≤h, and p is even with 4≤p≤P.

The polynomial formula accepts any deterministic direction tuple; only its unit-sphere restriction is used in the source-law theorem. Coefficients are arbitrary real tensor entries at this definition stage.
lesson.statement: Repeat each trailing direction K^j times, take p tensor copies, and pair their coordinates with a coefficient array. Multiply by the exact source amplitude √n a_i,p. A definition constructs this polynomial; it does not yet prove a probability law.
lesson.formula: \psi_i=u_i\otimes u_{i+1}^{\otimes K}\otimes\cdots\otimes u_h^{\otimes K^{h-i}},\qquad F_{i,p}^{\Xi}(u)=\sqrt n\,a_{i,p}\langle\Xi_{i,p},\psi_i(u)^{\otimes p}\rangle.
lesson.reader_note: The construction is folded below the theorem by default. It retains every multiplicity and constant; there is no symmetrized tensor, factorial normalization, or fallback branch.

steps.title: Name every tensor coordinate
steps.text: Write v_j=u_(i+j). A slot t=(r,j,k) chooses one of p copies, a trailing block j, and one of K^j repetitions. A coordinate c chooses one of n entries at every slot. Thus there are pS_i slots and n^(pS_i) coordinates; the feature entry is the product of the chosen direction coordinates.
steps.formula: \begin{gathered}T=\{(r,j,k):0\le r<p,\ 0\le j\le h-i,\ 0\le k<K^j\},\\ C=\{c:T\to\{0,\ldots,n-1\}\},\quad q_c=\prod_{t=(r,j,k)\in T}(v_j)_{c(t)},\\ |T|=pS_i,\qquad |C|=n^{pS_i}.\end{gathered}
steps.lean: Fin p × (Σ j, Fin(K^j)) is the finite slot type; a function from slots to Fin n is a coordinate. EuclideanSpace ℝ C uses the Euclidean norm, not the sup norm. The focused test proves the cardinality for arbitrary parameters.

steps.title: Keep the source amplitude
steps.text: Use the source values of K, P and S_i and the exact degree-dependent denominator. The j=0 summand gives S_i≥1; p≥4 and 2PS_i>1 make the denominator positive. The focused test proves positivity, so totalized division introduces no accidental zero value on this domain.
steps.lean: The body uses literal let-bindings for S and a. Positive dimension and the permitted degree subtype keep source constraints explicit; no estimated or renamed constant replaces a_i,p.

steps.title: Pair with the coefficient block
steps.text: Sum the coefficient entry times the matching tensor entry, then multiply by √n a_i,p. This is exactly the entrywise real tensor inner product. The formula extends polynomially off the sphere, but no off-sphere unit-norm assertion is made.
steps.lean: The finite sum in angularDegreeComponent is the literal coordinate pairing. Its deterministic polynomial extension has no conditional default and is not a new sampling algorithm.

lesson.lean_statement: The direction index starts at zero for the trailing tuple: Lean u j is the source u_(i+j). The coefficient type retains all ordered tensor coordinates.
lesson.lean_proof: This is a construction, not an inequality. The separate adjacent theorem derives its Gaussian law from the body.
lesson.dependency_notes: The finite coordinate carriers and arithmetic come from pinned Mathlib. No external Lean implementation is copied or given local proof credit.
